partially_covered.missing: Ontology provides hasAddress and hasIdentifier for organizations, but lacks explicit properties for displaying all organization details such as contact info, legal form, etc.
Ontology covers item, net price, and quantity but lacks explicit properties for item descriptions, product codes, and units of measure.
Ontology allows for invoice details via sections, but does not have explicit properties for all possible invoice details (e.g., payment terms, currency).

cq_coverage.details: Most CQs are fully covered via appropriate classes and properties. Partial gaps exist for detailed organization info, item attributes, and invoice detail granularity.

strengths: Rich and deep hierarchy reflecting EDIFACT structure
Good use of restrictions and equivalence
Clear reification for roles and item-invoice assignments
Disjointness and functional properties well defined
weaknesses: No GCAs for complex cross-class relationships
Limited modeling of detailed attributes (e.g., item descriptions, organization contact info)

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4: Missing domain/range for some inverse properties
reasoner_risks: Complex equivalence and intersection axioms may slow Hermit/Pellet but should not cause failures

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add explicit properties for organization details (e.g., hasContactInfo, hasLegalForm) and item attributes (e.g., hasDescription, hasProductCode, hasUnitOfMeasure) to fully cover CQ5 and CQ8.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improved CQ coverage and richer data modeling

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce General Class Axioms (GCAs) for validating relationships, such as ensuring that every Buyer role is linked to an Organization with a GLN identifier.
Expand invoice detail modeling with properties like hasPaymentTerms, hasCurrency, hasDueDate to fully address CQ10.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: More granular invoice information and better CQ coverage

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add example individuals and SHACL shapes for automated validation.

summary: This ontology demonstrates strong coverage of EDIFACT INVOIC structure and procurement roles, with robust class hierarchy and constraints. CQ coverage is high, but some questions are only partially addressed due to missing detailed properties. Quality is excellent overall; future improvements should focus on richer attribute modeling and GCAs for advanced validation.
